page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor configured with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via multithreading. Compute resources are dedicated, complemented by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per-vCPU ratio. It features no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Across benchmark evaluations, the ecs.r7t.2xlarge maintains average performance profiles across general compute tasks, scoring 1,546.0 on single-core and 5,655.0 on multi-core Geekbench suites. Memory throughput metrics register 423.1 GB/sec for small cached block reads, though uncached large-block reads decline to 33.45 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the lower 25% cohort for large memory transfers. In application testing, the instance achieved 7.96 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 12.06 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound machine learning tasks demonstrate moderate throughput on small language models, but processing capabilities decline significantly when running 7B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7t.2xlarge allocates a large memory envelope per vCPU without the premium cost of integrated hardware accelerators or bundled local NVMe arrays. The trade-off lies in its lower uncached memory read bandwidth and reliance on network-based block volumes for storage operations. This hardware footprint is technically aligned with in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational databases, enterprise applications, and medium-scale backend analytics engines that prioritize memory density over heavy uncached streaming or GPU compute.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual instance equipped with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. Configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, accompanied by a 48 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 instruction extensions. The instance includes no local storage volumes and relies on a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks show consistent mid-tier performance across single-core, multi-core, and encryption tests, reaching 7.96 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. However, large-block uncached memory read throughput remains relatively low. Given its resource balance and lack of bundled GPU or local NVMe storage, the ecs.r7t.2xlarge serves as a cost-efficient platform for in-memory databases, caching infrastructure, web applications, and memory-intensive enterprise services that require substantial system memory without specialized acceleration hardware.
